# Claude Code → Codex transition

**Researched 2026-08-21.** For a Claude Code power user running inside a
curated rootless-Podman OpenShell sandbox, evaluating a move to OpenAI Codex.
Drivers: cost/quota, model capability, harness effectiveness, cost to shift.

Full analysis: [claude-code-to-codex-transition.md](claude-code-to-codex-transition.md).
Sources: [citations.md](citations.md).

## The short version

Codex has reached broad feature parity — hooks, skills, subagents, plan mode,
an SDK, MCP, session resume, non-interactive execution [9][10][11][21][22][23].
The migration cost is concentrated in three places, and the two things you
actually want to know (is it cheaper, is it better) **cannot be answered from
published sources.** Both vendors decline to publish comparable quota, and the
standard coding benchmark was retracted by its own author [31]. Those questions
need a week of measurement, not more reading.

## What ports, what breaks

| Capability | Status | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Skills | **Equivalent** | `.claude/skills/` → `.agents/skills/`; `/name` → `$name` [21][53] |
| Plan mode | **Equivalent** | none [9] |
| Session resume | **Equivalent** | flag renames [9] |
| Non-interactive | **Equivalent+** | `claude -p` → `codex exec`; gains `--output-schema` [23] |
| SDK | **Equivalent** | `@openai/codex-sdk`, `openai-codex` [22] |
| MCP | **Equivalent** | JSON → TOML rewrite; loses elicitation hooks [13][52] |
| Subagents | **Partial** | every agent file rewritten Markdown → TOML [11] |
| **Hooks** | **Partial** | **11 events vs 31**; `command` handlers only; no `ask`, no tool-output rewrite [10][52] |
| **Permission rules** | **Different model** | `Tool(specifier)` arrays have no analogue — rewrite as permission profiles + execpolicy [14][53] |
| **Output styles** | **Weak** | three fixed `/personality` values [9] |
| Custom prompts | **Deprecated** | replaced by Skills, dated 2026-01-22 [6][12] |
| **OTel dashboards** | **Nothing carries** | disjoint namespaces `claude_code.*` vs `codex.*`; rebuild every panel [3][71][75] |
| **Cost telemetry** | **Regression** | Claude Code emits `claude_code.cost.usage` in USD; Codex emits no cost metric and no documented session tag on metrics [3][71] |

## The sandbox answer, in one quote

> "If the container is your intended security boundary, run Codex with
> `--sandbox danger-full-access` inside the container so Codex does not try to
> create a second sandbox layer." [20]

That is the `openshell-sandbox` design rule, restated by OpenAI. So
`--dangerously-skip-permissions` becomes
`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, and Codex's bwrap+seccomp sandbox
never has to be tested against rootless Podman.

**The real risk is the proxy, not the sandbox.** Codex's published
environment-variable list has twelve entries and **no proxy variable** [15]. The
PR that would have made `HTTPS_PROXY` explicit was closed unmerged in Oct 2025
[44]; its successor issue is still open [41]. If Codex ignores the injected
proxy variables it cannot reach the model at all through OpenShell's
CONNECT-only egress. **Test this before anything else** — it takes ten minutes.

## Decide in five steps

1. **Prove the proxy works** (10 min). Add a `codex_api` policy block —
   `api.openai.com`, `chatgpt.com`, `auth.openai.com`, `releases.openai.com`,
   port 443 — hot-apply it, `npm install -g @openai/codex`, log in with an API
   key, run `codex exec`. Every 403 names a host the policy is missing. This
   list is not published anywhere [69]; you are discovering it.
2. **Measure capability on your own work** (1 week). Re-run 5–8 tasks you
   already completed with Claude Code. Benchmarks cannot help — OpenAI itself
   says SWE-bench Verified "no longer reflect[s] meaningful improvements" [31].
3. **Measure cost on an API key, not a plan** (same week). Only API-key auth
   produces auditable numbers [4]. Compare **dollars per completed task**, never
   per token — Anthropic's tokenizer alone "produces approximately 30% more
   tokens for the same text" than its own predecessor [58].
4. **Price the harness rewrite** (half a day). Grep your hooks for the 20 events
   Codex lacks and for non-`command` handler types; count your permission rules
   and output styles. Then run `/import` and diff what actually arrived — that
   is the only way to find out what it migrates, because the page documenting it
   returns 404 [68].
5. **Decide.** Expect the middle outcome.

## Expect coexistence, not cutover

Both vendors' own ballparks overlap almost exactly — OpenAI "approximately
$100–$200 per developer per month" [33], Anthropic "$150-250 per developer per
month" [56]. If cost is the driver, published data does not promise a saving.

Coexistence is documented and cheap. Anthropic states it outright: "Claude Code
reads `CLAUDE.md`, not `AGENTS.md`… create a CLAUDE.md that imports it" [54].
Make `AGENTS.md` canonical, put `@AGENTS.md` at the top of `CLAUDE.md`, share
skills at `~/.agents/skills/` [21], and — for an OpenShell user — run each agent
in its own sandbox rather than fighting over one working tree, which neither
vendor documents. You pay twice [65]; while both tools ship this fast, that is a
reasonable hedge.

## If you run an OTel stack

Codex exports OTel properly — AWS ingests it into CloudWatch [86], OpenAI's
security blog shows a worked `[otel]` block [87], and OTLP/HTTP is first-class,
so a CONNECT proxy that cannot carry gRPC is fine [1][3]. Three things still
cost you:

1. **No dashboard survives.** `claude_code.*` and `codex.*` are disjoint
   namespaces [3][71][75]. The GenAI semantic conventions would have unified
   them but are still `Development` everywhere — 118 `Development` badges and
   zero `Stable` in the attribute registry, changelog reading only
   `## Unreleased`, and a releases page reading "There aren't any releases here"
   [79][80][81][82]. Codex emits zero `gen_ai.*` names; Claude Code emits six,
   spans only, one already deprecated [71][80].
2. **Cost telemetry regresses.** No Codex cost metric exists, and the documented
   metric tag set has no session identifier — so "what did this session cost"
   is not demonstrably answerable from Codex telemetry [3][71]. That is the
   exact measurement Step 3 above needs.
3. **Two default-on egress paths.** `otel.metrics_exporter` defaults to
   `statsig` [1], and anonymous analytics "default[s] to enabled, except in
   jurisdictions where opt-out is required by law" [76]. Set
   `analytics.enabled = false` and repoint the exporter, or add the hosts to
   your policy.

Full detail in [references/observability.md](references/observability.md).

## Two dates worth acting on

- **2026-08-31** — `gpt-5.4` and `gpt-5.4-mini` retire from Codex under ChatGPT
  sign-in; replacements are `gpt-5.6-terra` and `gpt-5.6-luna` [7].
- **Now** — Codex truncates its instruction chain at `project_doc_max_bytes`,
  **32 KiB by default** [5], where Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md "in full
  regardless of length" [54]. A shared instruction set can be silently truncated.
